notes.claim: In a pure inductor the voltage leads the current, that is, the current lags behind the voltage.
Inductive reactance is X_L = 2πfL, in ohms, and is directly proportional to the frequency of the alternating current.

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 3
sources.quote: Looking at the graph, the voltage wave seems to have a “head start” on the current wave; the voltage “leads” the current, and the current “lags” behind the voltage.

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 3
sources.quote: Inductive reactance can be calculated using this formula: X L = 2πfL

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 3
sources.quote: What this means is that reactance in ohms for any inductor is directly proportional to the frequency of the alternating current.
